title.character: Thomas's sister. Warm and plain; she wears the locket and trusts the room.
Mate of the Patience. Dry, one clouded eye, will not touch the book.
The baker on Bakery Row. Speaks through a door open a hand's width.
The board-keeper. Hands in a towel, his doorway lit, the bridge chain his.

Marsh's key to the shack padlock.
title.evidence: Thomas Voss, from Edith's folder. A clerk's coat, a careful face.
A tide-board peg cut VOSS, from the sluice grating.
title.idea: What is under the shack, which Marsh would not name at first.
The man under the streetlamp: an olive coat with brass buttons.
Marsh's word for Penry: where the hour will be read.
title.action-icon: Harlan Crowe, private inquiries. Shown, it opens doors.
title.note: Read his hour to her, in the office, at midnight. Leave the floor at berth four shut.
Tide clerk, twenty-eight. Berth four, the trawler Patience. Not to the water. Not in the rain.
Edith waits there until midnight. Grayhaven 3071.
Rang off at the turn of the tide and has not answered since. Grayhaven 214.
A. Penry, Bakery Row. Chalks the tide board and keeps the sluice chain.
The book is on the table. Leave the floor. The rain is not a room.
His name, an hour already passed, and her line: say it where the floor is dry.
